mostWorthwhile.text: Adding the sound-sensitive membranes was most worthwhile: the result explained how moving fluid bends hair-cell bundles and changes signals to nerve fibers, connecting the construction to its function.

leastWorthwhile.text: Joining the ears to the body was clear but predictable; it added less explanation than the earlier sensory-cell step.

surprise.text: I expected the hair cells to combine directly with the sound-sensitive membranes, but they had to go into the cochlear chambers first. The compatibility feedback made the next step clear.

arbitrary.text: The required order for assembling the hair cells and membranes initially felt arbitrary because both were described as belonging together in the cochlea.

continue.text: I would choose to continue if the next chapter similarly connects structures to what they do. The vibration-to-signal explanation held my interest, though several assembly steps were predictable.
